comparator.name: Bachelor Sociologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 ESSB EER specifies the complete 180-EC Sociology exam structure. The curriculum combines a broad first-year sociology/social-science foundation, qualitative and quantitative methods, a 15-EC internship, a 15-EC research project, a 15-EC minor, six substantive sociological-question areas, theoretical sociology, research-in-practice and a 15-EC bachelor project. No route selection is required.

alternatives.concept: A broad sociology-centred Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum combining social theory, qualitative and quantitative research, institutions, work, migration, identity and public communication.
basisLabels: Applied sociological research and public communication
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is anchored in the full UCR sociology sequence but also contains substantial politics, economics, history, psychology, methods and communication; the label therefore describes a broad sociology and social-research programme rather than a narrow subfield.

alternatives.concept: A sociology route organised around inequality, politics, law and public policy, with social research methods and historical context.
basisLabels: Applied sociological research and public communication
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines sociology with political science, law, public economics and historical analysis, so the visible label foregrounds politics, inequality and social change rather than presenting it as a conventional sociology major.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces part of the economics, psychology, sustainability and technology content with constitutional/EU law, additional political-institutional study and advanced history, creating a distinct policy-and-inequality organising logic.

alternatives.concept: A sociology route organised around planetary change, sustainability, technology and the transformation of work and institutions.
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines sociology with sustainability, climate, data, AI, organisations and politics, so the label states the society–sustainability–technology combination that actually dominates the programme.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This route replaces much of the law, history and conventional social-science breadth with sustainability, climate, programming, data and AI courses, producing a substantively different way of studying social change.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: Use the programme’s explicit inequality, politics, public-policy and social-change interests to organise a route around sociology, political institutions, law and redistribution.
candidateAssessments.assessment: Included as Alternative 2 because the evidence cluster is coherent, target-specific, mechanically feasible and produces substantially different course choices from the closest match.

candidateAssessments.candidateLabel: Planetary sociology, sustainability and technological change
candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: Use the programme’s explicit planetary-sociology, climate, technology and future-of-work interests to organise a route around social change, sustainability and digital systems.
candidateAssessments.assessment: Included as Alternative 3 because the evidence cluster is coherent, target-specific, feasible and clearly distinct from both the broad sociology route and the politics/policy route.

notes.text: The Erasmus Sociology programme contains a dedicated disciplinary sequence, a 15-EC internship and a 15-EC bachelor project. UCR can assemble substantial sociology and related social-science study, but it does not reproduce that fixed specialist structure or those components one-for-one.
